description: The image presents three pie charts from the paper “R2I-Bench: Benchmarking Reasoning-Driven Text-to-Image Generation,” each visualizing the proportional distribution of different reasoning categories within specific logical domains. The first chart, titled “Categorical,” divides into four segments: “Limiter” (27.91%, light pink), “Negation” (27.91%, orange), “Universal Quantifiers” (29.07%, light blue), and “Existential Quantifiers” (15.12%, light green), with the largest segment being Universal Quantifiers. The second chart, “Approximate Number Generation,” shows three segments: “Approximate Quantities” (45.03%, beige), “Comparative Relationships” (36.26%, light blue), and “Absolute Absence” (18.71%, lavender), with Approximate Quantities being the dominant category. The third chart, “Disjunctive & Conjunctive,” is nearly split in half between “Disjunctive” (49.51%, light lavender) and an unlabeled segment (50.49%, light pink) that visually corresponds to “Conjunctive,” as implied by the chart’s title. All charts display percentage values directly within each slice and use distinct pastel colors for visual differentiation, with no exploded segments or additional annotations beyond the labels and percentages.
